neet_phy_u12_t11_1.working: Balance condition: R/S = l/(100 - l). So 6/S = 40/60, giving S = 9 Ω.

neet_phy_u12_t11_2.working: Initially R/S = 25/75, so S = 3R. Shunting S by an equal resistance makes it S/2 = 1.5R. Then R/(1.5R) = l/(100 - l), so l/(100 - l) = 2/3 and l = 40 cm.

neet_phy_u12_t11_3.working: The null point depends only on the ratio R/S. Changing the cell emf, adding series resistance or changing galvanometer sensitivity leaves R/S unchanged. Heating S changes its resistance, so the null point shifts.

neet_phy_u12_t11_4.working: A: the wire is manganin or constantan (IV). B: interchanging R and S moves the null point from l to 100 - l (I). C: heating raises S, so l decreases and the point shifts towards R (II). D: shunting lowers S, so l increases and the point shifts towards S (III).

neet_phy_u12_t11_5.working: A is true: accuracy is best near 50 cm. B is false: the wire is manganin or constantan, not copper. C is true: this is the end-correction form. D is false: the jockey should be tapped, not slid while pressed. E is true: interchanging R and S and averaging reduces error. So A, C and E.
